Under the divider: two small charts, one for each trigger named in the sentence (ozone and fine particles as bars; warming, heat or cold as the temperature or feels-like line; falling pressure as the pressure line; humidity as its line or band), and when only one trigger is named, its chart is shown alone at full width (the condition’s usual two charts are used only when no trigger has a chart), side by side, always the same 44px height. Each has its name and the value now above it, followed by a small gray arrow for where it is heading over the next 3 hours (up arrow rising, down arrow falling, right arrow steady; steady means a change under 1 hPa for pressure, 1.5°C for temperature, 6 points for humidity, 5 ppb for ozone and 2 µg/m³ for fine particles; hover text says Rising, Falling or Steady over the next 3 hours; the air quality pill has no arrow), and (except the pill) a tiny light-gray time axis under it with a label every 6 hours at the clock hours (12a, 6a, 12p, 6p, 10px). Ozone and fine particles are scaled to today’s forecast so they agree with the ratings; a line is always at least a set height so a steady stretch reads flat.
